title: Microsoft BASIC for 6502 (V1.1) — Ben Eater board

programs.title: stored FOR/NEXT program
programs.input: 10 FOR I=1 TO 320 PRINT "HI";I30 NEXT IRUN

components.source: basic.s (ca65) built by fetch.sh; 32 KB ROM at $8000, vectors at $FFFA

historical.role: original macro source (not assemblable by modern tools; reference only)

buildable.role: ca65 translation with eater6502 W65C51 ACIA I/O

notes: Microsoft BASIC V1.1 for the 6502 (MIT, Microsoft's 2024 open-source release of m6502.asm), translated to ca65 and wired to the bw-board eater6502 machine's W65C51 ACIA console at $5000. Drop basic.rom into the eater6502 `rom` slot: the machine boots, prompts MEMORY SIZE? and WIDTH? over the ACIA, then prints its BYTES FREE line and the 'MICROSOFT BASIC V1.1 / COPYRIGHT 1978 MICROSOFT' banner and the OK prompt (this V1.1 uses OK, not the later READY.). It is a full interactive BASIC: type a line to enter it, RUN to run it. The `programs[]` here are scripted ACIA sessions (`input` is the bytes typed in, `expect` what the machine prints back); proof.mjs replays them through bw-board's runMediaBundle. The leading carriage returns in each `input` answer the two boot prompts with defaults. Verified reproducible: fetch.sh rebuilds basic.rom byte-for-byte from the pinned ca65 source.
